title: Loops and arrays
objectives: hold many values in an array
say why a typed array refuses the wrong value

steps.instruction: An array holds many values under one name.
body: number[] means an array of numbers.
Positions start at 0, so scores[0] is the first.

steps.instruction: Try to push the text "100" onto this array of numbers.
steps.after: The array was declared to hold numbers, so text is refused.

steps.instruction: Repeat a fixed number of times.
body: Start at 0, keep going while i is under 3, add one each pass.

steps.instruction: Print the numbers 1 to 5, one per line.
steps.hint: Start at 1 and keep going while i <= 5.
steps.after: Where you start and when you stop are both yours to choose.

body: Each pass hands you the next value.
No index, no length, nothing to get wrong.
steps.keypoint: for (const item of array) — when you do not need the position.

skills: add up an array with for...of

steps.instruction: Print each name in capitals, one per line.
steps.after: TypeScript knows n is a string, so toUpperCase is allowed.

body: Use while when you do not know how many passes it takes.
Something inside must change, or it never stops.
steps.keypoint: while (test) { ... } — the test must eventually become false.

body: Start empty, add as you go.
steps.keypoint: arr.push(value) adds one to the end.

steps.hint: The values are text. Each pass gives you one word. total collects.
steps.after: string[] for text, of to walk it, += to collect.

steps.instruction: Count how many scores are 50 or more, and print that count.
steps.hint: A counter starting at 0, a for...of loop, and an if inside it.
steps.after: A counter, a loop and a test. That pattern turns up constantly.
